insurer: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: ₹2 lakhs / ₹3 lakhs / ₹4 lakhs / ₹5 lakhs / ₹7 lakhs / ₹10 lakhs

good.name: PED Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months (48 months for plans with Sum Insured up to 2Lacs) of continuous coverage
good.reference: Policy Wordings Part II, Clause 3.1 (Code-Excl01) / Key Information Sheet: Waiting Period (a)
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are excluded for 24 months for most sum insured options, and 48 months for plans with ₹2 lakh sum insured. This means you must wait up to 2 years (or 4 years for lower SI) before claims for pre-existing conditions are covered.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage
good.reference: Policy Wordings Part II, Clause 3.2 (Code-Excl02) / Key Information Sheet: Waiting Period (b)
good.explanation: Treatment for specified diseases and procedures is excluded for 24 months from policy start. This standard waiting period delays coverage for certain illnesses and surgeries.

good.name: Initial Waiting
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.reference: Policy Wordings Part II, Clause 3.4 (Code-Excl03) / Key Information Sheet: Waiting Period (d)
good.explanation: Illnesses are not covered during the first 30 days of the policy, but accidents are covered immediately. This is a common waiting period to prevent immediate claims.

good.name: Restore Benefit
good.quote: For plans with Sum Insured ` 3lacs and above, We will reset up to 100% of the Sum insured once in a policy year... The reset amount can only be used for all future claims within the same policy year, not related to the illness/ disease/ injury for which a claim has been paid in that policy year for the same person
good.reference: Policy Wordings Part II, Section 2 (Scope of Cover), (E) Reset Benefit / Key Information Sheet: Reset Benefit
good.explanation: The sum insured is restored once per policy year for plans ₹3 lakh and above, but only for new illnesses or injuries. This helps increase coverage but does not cover repeated claims for the same condition.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization
good.quote: Pre-hospitalisation Medical Expenses incurred by You for a 30-day period immediately prior to Your Hospitalisation
good.reference: Policy Wordings Part II, Section 2 (C) Pre-Hospitalisation and Post-Hospitalisation Expenses / Key Information Sheet: Pre & Post Hospitalisation
good.explanation: Medical expenses up to 30 days before hospitalization are covered. This helps cover diagnostic tests and treatments leading to hospital admission.

good.name: Post-hospitalization
good.quote: Post-hospitalisation Medical Expenses incurred by You for a 60-day period immediately post Hospitalisation
good.reference: Policy Wordings Part II, Section 2 (C) Pre-Hospitalisation and Post-Hospitalisation Expenses / Key Information Sheet: Pre & Post Hospitalisation
good.explanation: Medical expenses up to 60 days after discharge are covered. This supports recovery costs and follow-up treatments after hospitalization.

good.name: No Claim Bonus
good.quote: An Additional Sum Insured of 10% of Annual Sum Insured provided on each renewal for every claim-free year up to a maximum of 50%. In case of a claim under the policy, the accumulated Additional Sum Insured will be reduced by 10% of the Annual Sum Insured in the following year.
good.reference: Key Information Sheet: Renewal Benefits (a) / Policy Wordings Part II, Section 2 (G) Additional Sum Insured (Cumulative Bonus)
good.explanation: Sum insured increases by 10% for each claim-free year up to 50%, and reduces by 10% after a claim instead of resetting to zero. This rewards claim-free renewals with extra coverage.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Below are the non payable items applicable in the policy... List of Non Payable Items as per IRDAI... 56 GLOVES ... 60 MASK ... 57 NEBULISATION KIT ... 58 RECOVERY KIT, ETC]ANY KIT WITH NO DETAILS MENTIONED
bad.reference: Policy Wordings: Non Payables (List of Non Payable Items as per IRDAI)
bad.explanation: Many consumables like gloves, masks, and kits are excluded from coverage. This means you may have to pay these common hospital items out of pocket.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits
bad.quote: (a) Cataract, where sub-limit of ` 20,000/- is applicable per eye per Policy year for Plans with Sum Insured up to 5 Lacs... (b) Sub limit options of A and B available for Sum Insured option 2 lacs and Sub limit C option is available for 3 lacs/ 4 lacs/ 5 lacs
bad.reference: Key Information Sheet: Sub Limit (a), (b) / Policy Wordings Clause 3.2 and Extension 15 (Sub Limits)
bad.explanation: Specific diseases like cataract have rupee sub-limits (e.g., ₹20,000 per eye), which can restrict claim amounts. This limits your payout for common treatments.

bad.name: Cashless Network
bad.quote: Cashless Facility available at over 4000+ network hospitals.
bad.reference: Key Information Sheet: Payout Basis / Claim Administration
bad.explanation: The cashless hospital network includes about 4,000 hospitals, fewer than many competitors offering 7,000–10,000+. This may limit your cashless options.

bad.name: Restore Benefit
bad.reference: Key Information Sheet: Clause 2. Scope of the Cover (Reset Benefit)
bad.explanation: The ₹2 lakh sum insured plan does not offer any restore/reset benefit, so your coverage is not replenished after a claim within the policy year.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: Co-payment means a cost sharing requirement under a health insurance policy that provides that the policyholder/insured/proposer will bear a specified percentage of the admissible claims amount.
bad.explanation: Co-pay is defined but the policy does not clearly state if or what percentage applies by default. Confirm co-pay details in your policy schedule.

unclear.name: Room Rent
unclear.quote: Room Rent means the amount charged by a hospital for the occupancy of a bed on per day (24 hours) basis and shall include associated medical expenses.
unclear.reference: Policy Wordings Part II: Definitions (Room Rent)
unclear.explanation: The policy defines room rent but does not specify the eligible room category or any capping. Check your policy schedule for exact room rent limits.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
